items.t: ALMA Reveals a Dying Star's Final Breath, Encoded In a Giant Ring of Gas

items.t: A New Discovery is Re-Drawing the Map of the Milky Way
items.sum: New research shows that star formation is occurring in the Milky Way's central bar. This goes against previous research, and against observations of other barred spiral galaxies. The discovery by a PhD student shows a vast rotating structure of stars near the centre of our Galaxy is driving enormous shock fronts through clouds of gas, compressing them and creating conditions for new stars to form.

items.t: Maybe Dark Energy Isn't so Inexplicable After All
items.sum: The Universe as we know it is comprised of three "things": baryonic matter (planets, stars, galaxies, us), dark matter (still unexplained) and dark energy (really, really still unexplained). Of the three, dark energy remains challenging because it's driving the acceleration of the expanding Universe. However, we can't see it, or even put a description to it, other than, "it's mysterious".

items.t: A Gigantic Stellar Eruption Spreads Planetary Material Into Space
items.sum: Asymptotic Giant Branch (AGB) stars spread heavy elements into space with their stellar winds. This material eventually forms more stars, and even rocky planets like ours. For a long time, astronomers thought this important mass-loss was driven by stellar winds. But new research shows how magnetic fields play an important role. A vast flare and magnetic loop of material from the AGB star Mira provides the evidence.

items.t: Science Release: Astronomers Discover Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua, the Oldest Compact Quasar Pair in the Universe
items.sum: The oldest pair of compact quasars ever observed has been found only 900 million years after the Big Bang. Scientists say there is no theoretical explanation for how the pair of actively feeding black holes grew so massive at such an early time in the history of the Universe. The pair of quasars has been given the Hawaiian name Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua.
